goal: Determine the smallest generic Inventory runtime that makes lookup and append outcomes attributable and reproducible across installed repositories without turning Inventory into authority or hiding historical debt.
context: The live Inventory index is lookup-ready, but clean adds re-emit 72 inherited tag warnings, the installed package lacks its documented validator pair, and conformance observations can outlive the index digest they describe. The candidate runtime should resolve a package-local validator, capture before and after digests, separate introduced from inherited warnings, and emit one deterministic non-authority operation receipt. Ashby runs formal ownership analysis while Spivak runs executable data-flow analysis and Wiener runs operator-portability analysis; for every pair, a contract-only, fixture-only, or UX-only bias is exposed by the other methodology. Rittel attacks precedent while Popper attacks non-vacuity and Wittgenstein attacks definitional collapse; for every pair, an already-owned, unwitnessed, or merely renamed runtime is exposed by the other attack-vector.
anti_bias_global: runtime improvement must survive both construction-method diversity and independent collapse gates

groups.anti_bias: composite methodology and source-corpus: formal contract archaeology vs computational failure modeling vs operator-centered portability. Ashby runs formal contract archaeology, Spivak runs computational failure modeling on the methodology axis; a contract-only bias in Ashby would be exposed by Spivak's executable fixtures. Ashby runs formal contract archaeology, Wiener runs adversarial operator-portability analysis on the methodology axis; a contract-only bias in Ashby would be exposed by Wiener's consumer failure paths. Spivak runs computational failure modeling, Wiener runs adversarial operator-portability analysis on the methodology axis; a fixture-only bias in Spivak would be exposed by Wiener's install, path-resolution, and operator-use failures.

agents.angle: formal contract archaeology over canonical public ownership, installed adapter ownership, bootstrap, synchronization, and authority boundaries
agents.initial_prompt: Design the ownership and lifecycle contract for a generic Inventory runtime. Inspect the canonical Inventory source, bootstrap/sync/runtime-composition owners, the current maintenance reflection, and the selected Inventory entries sigil-maintenance-loop-inventory-first-hardening and domainspec-subagents-research-review-inventory-preflight. Return: candidate runtime boundaries, public versus consumer-owned files, invocation states, authority exclusions, compatibility risks, and exact source selectors. Do not edit files and do not treat Inventory as authority.

agents.angle: computational failure modeling over updater, validator, digest, warning-delta, idempotence, and receipt fixtures
agents.initial_prompt: Derive an executable data-flow model for a generic Inventory operation receipt. Reproduce or inspect the whole-index warning behavior, validator pair dependency, dry-run semantics, and current reflection evidence. Return: input/output schema, baseline-to-candidate warning-delta algorithm, digest binding, failure states, idempotence rules, and minimal deterministic fixtures. Use most-used-skills-efficiency-review-strategy-result only as a discovery lead and verify the current code. Do not edit files.

agents.angle: adversarial operator-centered portability across install, validate, lookup, append, observe, repair, and standalone consumer failure paths
agents.initial_prompt: Model how an operator and consuming repository would use an Inventory runtime without knowing the upstream Arcanum checkout. Inspect installed package layout, documented lookup commands, observer hooks, and synchronization behavior. Return: smallest CLI or profile surface, path-resolution and dependency rules, fail-closed messages, operator receipt UX, migration path, and portability tests. Preserve the 72 historical warnings as visible debt but prevent them from being attributed to every clean operation. Do not edit files.

Reconcile the three explorer returns into candidate Inventory runtime designs. Produce a smallest viable contract with states, commands, receipt schema, canonical-versus-installed ownership, synchronization mechanics, test matrix, migration phases, and explicit exclusions. Cite every load-bearing statement to an explorer return or a verified source. Keep alternative candidates separate so the skeptics can kill redundant or unwitnessed designs.

groups.anti_bias: attack-vector: precedent vs vacuity vs definitional. Rittel runs precedent attack, Popper runs vacuity attack on the attack-vector axis; a precedent-only bias in Rittel would be exposed by Popper's demand for closed witnesses. Rittel runs precedent attack, Wittgenstein runs definitional attack on the attack-vector axis; an already-owned bias in Rittel would be exposed if Wittgenstein shows the candidate merely renames an existing owner. Popper runs vacuity attack, Wittgenstein runs definitional attack on the attack-vector axis; a witness-only bias in Popper would be exposed if Wittgenstein shows the witnessed candidate has no unique responsibility.

agents.angle: precedent attack: find the actual existing Arcanum or external owner before accepting a new runtime surface
agents.initial_prompt: Attack the synthesis through the precedent gate. Verify whether observed-invocation-loop, signal-observer, arcanum-bootstrap, Inventory validators, runtime profiles, package managers, or established CLI receipt patterns already own each proposed capability. Label each candidate build-from-owned, already-deployed, or precedent-clean with citations. Precedent does not emit KILL.

agents.angle: non-vacuity attack: force concrete clean-add, new-warning, missing-helper, stale-digest, and no-mutation witnesses
agents.initial_prompt: Attack the synthesis through the non-vacuity gate. Hand-construct the smallest fixtures for a clean controlled append over historical debt, one introduced warning, a missing validator helper, a stale receipt digest, and repeated dry runs. Require exact expected status, receipt fields, stdout/stderr, and mutation behavior. KILL any candidate that cannot produce a closed witness.

agents.angle: definitional attack: test whether the proposed runtime is only a renamed updater, validator, observer, or maintenance spell
agents.initial_prompt: Attack the synthesis through the definitional-soundness gate. Compare every candidate with the existing updater, full validator, signal observer, observed invocation loop, bootstrap/sync tooling, and maintenance spell. Demand a unique owned responsibility and explicit non-responsibilities. KILL any candidate that collapses to a renamed wrapper or duplicates an existing owner.

Write findings.md only from the explorer transcript, synthesis, and skeptic returns. Include the candidate verdict matrix with owner, witnessed, sound, and verdict columns; one recommended minimal runtime; rejected alternatives; exact public/private ownership; deterministic receipt schema; implementation slices; validation gates; and claim-to-source citations. Preserve Inventory as a non-authority read model.

Audit findings.md against the dispatch goal. Approve only if the verdict matrix is complete, every load-bearing claim is cited, the recommended runtime has a concrete witness and a unique owner, package-local validation is reproducible, historical warnings remain visible but attributable, Inventory authority does not expand, and public Arcanum contains no private checkout bindings. Otherwise return exact revision requests.
